notes: English version of junior.json: same ids, same option order (correct/funny indexes come from the RU file).
Adapted, not literal: local references and jokes are replaced with English equivalents.

questions.question: UX is how it feels to use a product. Colors, fonts and the look of buttons are…
questions.explanation: UX is the whole experience: is it clear, is it easy, did it get the job done. UI is what you see and tap. A pretty UI won't save a clumsy flow.

questions.question: A prototype of gray boxes labeled “photo here” is…
questions.explanation: Low-fi tests the idea and structure; high-fi tests details, visuals and motion.

questions.question: Which Figma property rounds the corners of a button?
questions.explanation: Corner radius sets the rounding; each corner can have its own value.

questions.question: Who created Material Design?
questions.explanation: Material Design was introduced in 2014; the current version is Material 3.

questions.question: A layout rearranges by screen width: 3 columns on tablet, 1 on phone. This is…
questions.explanation: A fluid layout just stretches without rearranging. A mobile version is a separate site.

questions.question: Where in Figma do you set up a screen transition on click?
questions.explanation: In the Prototype tab you connect screens and set the transition animation.

questions.question: How do you make a button grow with its text?
questions.explanation: Hug fits the content, Fill takes all available space, Fixed keeps a set size.

questions.question: You changed the main component. What happens to its instances?
questions.explanation: Except for properties you've overridden in a specific instance.

questions.question: A set of font sizes with a constant ratio (×1.25) is a…
questions.explanation: A scale gives clear hierarchy: heading, subheading, body, caption.

questions.question: Why shouldn't long text be set in ALL CAPS?
questions.explanation: Lowercase letters differ in shape, so the eye recognizes words by their outline. Solid caps read slower.

questions.question: An error is shown only with a red border. Who will struggle?
questions.explanation: Add error text or an icon. By the way, bulls barely see red — it's the moving cape that annoys them.

questions.question: Why does a designer need a persona?
questions.explanation: A good persona is built on research, not fantasy. And “Karen, 34” is not to blame.

questions.question: What is a UI kit?
questions.explanation: A UI kit speeds up work and keeps the interface consistent. A design system is a UI kit plus rules and processes.

questions.question: Which format is best for icons that must stay sharp on any screen?
questions.explanation: SVG is vector: it scales without quality loss and weighs little.

questions.question: What makes PNG better than JPG for UI graphics?
questions.explanation: JPG is good for photos; PNG is for graphics with transparency and crisp edges.

questions.question: Linked screens you can “walk through” like a real app are a…
questions.explanation: A clickable prototype is tested with users before development.

questions.question: A window over the page that blocks it until closed is a…
questions.explanation: Modals interrupt the user — use them for things that really matter.

questions.question: A screen with no data yet and a hint on what to do is an…
questions.explanation: A good empty state explains what will be here and leads to the first action.

questions.question: Error 404 means…
questions.explanation: A server error is 500, no access is 403. A good 404 helps you find what you need.

questions.question: What is onboarding?
questions.explanation: Onboarding should get the user to the first value fast, not show off every feature.

questions.question: Which color most often signals an error in interfaces?
questions.explanation: But never show an error by color alone — add text or an icon.

questions.question: Why does a button need a disabled state?
questions.explanation: Ideally, it's clear nearby why the button is unavailable and what to do.

questions.question: Hover is the state when…
questions.explanation: Pressing is pressed/active; keyboard focus is focus.

questions.question: Is there hover on a touchscreen?
questions.explanation: Don't hide important things behind hover — phone users will never see them.

questions.question: A trick that pushes users into a choice against their interest is a…
questions.explanation: Like a hidden subscription or “No, I don't like discounts”. It hurts trust and reputation.

questions.question: The tiny site icon in a browser tab is a…
questions.explanation: Short for favorites icon — it used to show up in Favorites.

questions.question: What are fonts without serifs called?
questions.explanation: Serif fonts have the little feet; sans-serif fonts don't.

questions.question: The spacing between a specific pair of letters is…
questions.explanation: Even spacing across all letters is tracking.

questions.question: Leading is the space…
questions.explanation: In CSS it's line-height.

questions.question: Navigation like “Home › Courses › UX” is called…
questions.explanation: It shows where you are and lets you jump a level up.

questions.question: CTA stands for Call to…
questions.explanation: Call to Action: “Buy”, “Start”. A cat calls too, but for something else.

questions.question: In the popular “8pt grid”, sizes and spacing are multiples of…
questions.explanation: 8 divides well and scales cleanly at ×1.5, ×2 and ×3 densities.

questions.question: Why does an image need an alt attribute?
questions.explanation: Decorative images get an empty alt so screen readers skip them.

questions.question: Gray blocks in place of content while loading are a…
questions.explanation: Skeletons show the structure upfront, so the wait feels shorter.

questions.question: A map of a customer's steps, thoughts and feelings from first touch to purchase is a…
questions.explanation: A Customer Journey Map shows the whole path: where the customer is happy and where they're ready to quit.

questions.question: A usability test participant is stuck. What does the moderator do?
questions.explanation: The moderator doesn't help: a hint hides the real problem. You can ask “What did you expect to see?”

questions.question: A diagram of steps to a goal: screen → action → next screen is a…
questions.explanation: A user flow shows the path step by step and helps cut extra screens before drawing.

questions.question: How a site's sections are organized, labeled and linked is its information…
questions.explanation: Information architecture answers “where is everything and how do I find it”.

questions.question: A progress bar shows the process is running. Which Nielsen heuristic is it?
questions.explanation: Heuristic #1, visibility of system status: always tell users what's going on, in time and clearly.

questions.question: A menu shows options instead of making you remember them. This is…
questions.explanation: Recognizing beats recalling: keep options in sight, not in the user's head.

questions.question: Who writes button labels, error messages and hints in an interface?
questions.explanation: A UX writer owns microcopy: from “Save” to explaining an error like a human.

questions.question: Where should “Invalid email” appear in a form?
questions.explanation: An error next to the field shows exactly what to fix and where.

questions.question: The user reached the goal with no errors or detours. Which scenario is this?
questions.explanation: The happy path is the most common route to the goal. Alternatives and errors come next, or the product breaks at the first detour.

questions.question: Software that reads the interface aloud for blind users is a…
questions.explanation: A screen reader voices text, buttons and labels. Without labels it reads “button, button, button”.

questions.question: How do you move to the next button on a site without a mouse?
questions.explanation: Tab moves focus between elements. Everything that works with a mouse must work with a keyboard.

questions.question: Design for the small screen first, then expand. This approach is…
questions.explanation: A small screen forces you to pick what matters — it's easier to add later than to cut.

questions.question: Eyes scan text in two horizontal bars, then down the left edge. This is the…
questions.explanation: In the F-pattern, line starts and first paragraphs get read, the rest gets scanned. Put key info first.

questions.question: You need 500 users' opinions on a new feature. Which method fits?
questions.explanation: A survey gives numbers and scale. Interviews give depth with 5–10 people.

questions.question: Same elements look and work the same on every screen. This is…
questions.explanation: Nielsen's heuristic #4, consistency and standards: users shouldn't have to guess.

questions.question: After submitting a form, users see “Request received”. Why?
questions.explanation: Without confirmation people aren't sure it worked and submit again.

questions.question: The feed loads new posts automatically when you reach the end. This is…
questions.explanation: Great for feeds, bad for search: the footer is unreachable and you can't get back to a spot.

questions.question: How do you cut the effort of entering a delivery address?
questions.explanation: Address suggestions and browser autofill save time and reduce errors.

questions.question: A description of how a user completes a specific task with a product is a…
questions.explanation: A use case: who, why and in what steps. It helps you not forget alternative paths.

questions.question: What do you call a research participant who answers questions?
questions.explanation: The respondent answers; the moderator runs the session and asks questions.

questions.question: Why does an icon without a label need a label or tooltip?
questions.explanation: Only a few icons are clear on their own: home, search, cart. People read the rest differently.

questions.question: Subtitles for videos in a product are primarily for…
questions.explanation: For deaf and hard-of-hearing people subtitles are the only access to sound. For everyone else, a bonus on the subway.

questions.question: By the ISO standard, usability is effectiveness, efficiency and…
questions.explanation: ISO 9241-11: how well, at what cost and with what feeling the user reaches the goal.

questions.question: A prototype hand-drawn on sheets of paper is a…
questions.explanation: The fastest way to test an idea: redrawing a sheet is cheaper than redoing a mockup.

questions.question: Which color model do screens use?
questions.explanation: Screens emit red, green and blue light. CMYK is for printing with ink.

questions.question: Which color is #FFFFFF?
questions.explanation: All three channels at max (FF = 255) make white. #000000 is black.

questions.question: Colors opposite each other on the color wheel are…
questions.explanation: A complementary pair gives maximum contrast, like blue and orange.

questions.question: How should long article text be aligned to be easy to read?
questions.explanation: A straight left edge helps the eye find the start of each line. Justified text on the web leaves gaps between words.

questions.question: An icon of three horizontal lines that opens a menu is a…
questions.explanation: Hamburger is three lines, kebab is three vertical dots, meatball is three horizontal dots.

questions.question: A short notice at the bottom of the screen that disappears by itself is a…
questions.explanation: A toast (snackbar) doesn't block work and leaves on its own. Not for important stuff — it's easy to miss.

questions.question: You need to pick exactly one option out of three. Which control fits?
questions.explanation: Radio buttons: one of several. Checkboxes: any number.

questions.question: How is a toggle switch different from a checkbox?
questions.explanation: A toggle applies the setting at once, like a light switch. A checkbox usually needs “Save”.

questions.question: The space from a button's edge to its text is…
questions.explanation: Padding is inner spacing; margin is outer spacing to neighboring elements.

questions.question: What in Figma sets how a layer behaves when its frame is resized?
questions.explanation: Constraints pin a layer to the frame's edges or center, so it moves or stretches on resize.

questions.question: The image broke into little squares when zoomed in. So it is…
questions.explanation: Raster is made of pixels, vector of formulas — that's why vector scales without loss.

questions.question: The main thing is big and bold, the secondary smaller and quieter. This is…
questions.explanation: Hierarchy controls reading order: size, weight, color and spacing say what matters more.

questions.question: Empty space around elements that lets a layout “breathe” is…
questions.explanation: White (negative) space groups and highlights — it isn't “empty”.

questions.question: A list that opens on click and lets you choose an option is a…
questions.explanation: A dropdown hides options until clicked. With 2–3 options, better show them right away.

questions.question: A person interested in the product who influences decisions is a…
questions.explanation: Stakeholders: client, management, legal, support. Learn their expectations before the mockups.

questions.question: The share of visitors who completed the target action is…
questions.explanation: Out of 1,000 visitors, 30 bought — that's 3% conversion.

questions.question: DAU is how many unique users were active in the product within…
questions.explanation: Daily Active Users: unique users active within a day, even if they came only once. MAU is per month.

questions.question: A list of product tasks and ideas sorted by priority is a…
questions.explanation: A backlog is a living list: what's on top gets picked up first.

questions.question: A short fixed work cycle of a team in Scrum is a…
questions.explanation: A sprint usually lasts 1–4 weeks and ends with a working increment.

questions.question: An approach where stages go strictly one after another, no going back, is…
questions.explanation: Waterfall: requirements → design → development → testing. A mistake made early is found at the very end.

questions.question: Two versions of a screen are shown to different people and compared. This is…
questions.explanation: An A/B test answers “which version wins on the metric” but doesn't explain why.

questions.question: “As a shopper, I want to save my cart so that…” is the format of a…
questions.explanation: A user story: who, what they want and why. The focus is on value, not buttons.

questions.question: The answer to “why would a customer choose us over a competitor” is…
questions.explanation: A value proposition: what problem we solve and why we beat the alternatives.

questions.question: A short daily team meeting about task status is a…
questions.explanation: The daily (daily scrum) is 15 minutes on plans and blockers, not a report to the boss.

questions.question: Who coined the term “user experience” while working at Apple in the 90s?
questions.explanation: Don Norman became Apple's “User Experience Architect” in 1993 — and the term went global.

questions.question: What is the iPhone's built-in screen reader called?
questions.explanation: VoiceOver is on iOS and macOS; TalkBack is on Android.

questions.question: A big dropdown panel showing all sections and subsections at once is a…
questions.explanation: A mega menu suits large catalogs: everything is visible at once, no nested dropdowns.

questions.question: A persona built from the team's guesses without research is a…
questions.explanation: A proto-persona is a hypothesis. Useful for a start, but it must be checked with real people.

questions.question: Participants log their experience with a product for weeks. This is a…
questions.explanation: A diary study catches habits and context you can't see in an hour-long interview.

questions.question: A researcher watches someone work right at their workplace. This is…
questions.explanation: Contextual inquiry: people describe their work poorly but show it well.

questions.question: You check where people click first to complete a task. This is a… test
questions.explanation: If the first click is right, people complete the task in about 87% of cases.

questions.question: Users ignore blocks that look like ads. This is…
questions.explanation: The brain learned to filter out ads — and everything that looks like them.

questions.question: The ISO standard on human-centred design of systems:
questions.explanation: ISO 9241-210 describes the cycle: context → requirements → solutions → evaluation.

questions.question: Empathy map: what the user says, thinks, does and…
questions.explanation: Four quadrants: Says, Thinks, Does, Feels. The gaps between them are the interesting part.

questions.question: “Any page within three clicks.” What is this, according to research?
questions.explanation: Research shows people don't quit after three clicks if every step is clear.

questions.question: Up to what delay does a system response feel instant (per Nielsen)?
questions.explanation: 0.1 s feels instant, 1 s keeps the flow of thought, 10 s is the limit of attention.

questions.question: Interview insights are grouped on sticky notes by meaning. What's this method?
questions.explanation: An affinity diagram turns hundreds of observations into a few themes.

questions.question: The cycle “research → design → test → repeat” is…
questions.explanation: Each iteration refines the solution with data, not guesses.

questions.question: A style imitating real materials — leather, wood, glass — is…
questions.explanation: Early iOS was skeuomorphic: a leather calendar, wooden iBooks shelves.

questions.question: How many pixels is 1rem if the user hasn't changed browser settings?
questions.explanation: rem is based on the root font size; browsers default to 16 px.

questions.question: In the HSL color model, H stands for…
questions.explanation: Hue is the tone (an angle on the wheel), Saturation is intensity, Lightness is brightness.

questions.question: The golden ratio is approximately…
questions.explanation: φ ≈ 1.618. 1.414 is √2, the aspect ratio of an A4 sheet.

questions.question: Two letters joined into one glyph, like “fi”, is a…
questions.explanation: A ligature replaces a letter pair with one glyph so they don't collide.

questions.question: The default system font of Android and Material Design is…
questions.explanation: Roboto is the font of Android and Material; SF Pro is Apple's system font.

questions.question: Which Figma boolean operation cuts the top shape out of the bottom one?
questions.explanation: Union merges, Intersect keeps the overlap, Exclude keeps everything but it.

questions.question: What is the Figma mode for developers, with spacing and code, called?
questions.explanation: Dev Mode shows sizes, spacing, variables and code snippets for development.

questions.question: Which icon marks a component instance in Figma's layers panel?
questions.explanation: An instance is a diamond outline, a main component is four diamonds, a frame is a #.

questions.question: Colors that sit next to each other on the color wheel are…
questions.explanation: Analogous colors give calm harmony; complementary ones give contrast.

questions.question: A frosted-glass effect with the background blurred under a panel is…
questions.explanation: Glassmorphism relies on background blur, translucency and a thin light border.

questions.question: Soft buttons “pressed” out of the background with two shadows are…
questions.explanation: Pretty on Dribbble, but neumorphism has weak contrast — buttons are hard to spot.

questions.question: What is screen pixel density measured in?
questions.explanation: PPI is pixels per inch. FPS and hertz are about frame rate.

questions.question: Why export images at @2x?
questions.explanation: On high-density screens 1 point = 2 pixels, so a @1x image looks blurry.

questions.question: Important/urgent — four quadrants for priorities. Whose matrix is it?
questions.explanation: The Eisenhower matrix: important and urgent — now; important, not urgent — plan; the rest — delegate or drop.

questions.question: Who owns the product backlog in Scrum?
questions.explanation: The Product Owner orders the backlog; the Scrum Master helps the team work by Scrum.

questions.question: A board with “To do / In progress / Done” columns is a…
questions.explanation: Kanban shows the flow of tasks, so you can see where they get stuck.

questions.question: The share of users who left the product over a period is…
questions.explanation: Churn rate is measured per period, e.g. 5% a month. Keeping a user is usually cheaper than getting a new one.

questions.question: The cost of acquiring one customer is the metric…
questions.explanation: CAC is Customer Acquisition Cost: marketing and sales spend divided by the number of new customers.

questions.question: A user pays every month for access to a service. This model is a…
questions.explanation: Subscriptions bring regular income but require proving value all the time — or churn.

questions.question: An end-of-sprint meeting where the team discusses how to work better is a…
questions.explanation: A retrospective is about the process; a demo is about the result for the client.

questions.question: The “Buy” button got bigger and closer to the thumb — easier to hit. Whose law?
questions.explanation: The bigger and closer the target, the faster you hit it.

questions.question: People expect your site to work like the ones they're used to. Whose law?
questions.explanation: Jakob Nielsen: users spend most of their time on other sites.

questions.question: “Delete project?” with a confirmation — which Nielsen heuristic is it?
questions.explanation: Heuristic #5: better to prevent a mistake than to report it nicely.

questions.question: How many usability heuristics did Jakob Nielsen define?
questions.explanation: Formulated in 1990 with Rolf Molich, refined in 1994.

questions.question: According to Nielsen, how many participants are enough for a qualitative test?
questions.explanation: Five find about 85% of problems; several small tests beat one big one.

questions.question: A participant says out loud everything they think while doing a task. Method:
questions.explanation: Think aloud is the main usability-testing tool according to Nielsen.

questions.question: Participants sort cards with section names into groups. Method:
questions.explanation: It helps build navigation the way users see it.

questions.question: WCAG principles: perceivable, operable, understandable and…
questions.explanation: POUR — Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust.

questions.question: Gray hint text inside a field vanishes as soon as you type. This is a…
questions.explanation: NN/g: a placeholder doesn't replace a label — it disappears while typing.

questions.question: Ctrl+Z saves you from an accidental action. What's this feature called?
questions.explanation: Nielsen's heuristic #3: users need an “emergency exit” — undo and redo.

questions.question: WCAG AA: what minimum contrast does normal text need?
questions.explanation: Large text needs 3:1; level AAA needs 7:1.

questions.question: Minimum tap target per Apple HIG:
questions.explanation: The icon can be smaller, but the touch area should be at least 44×44 pt.

questions.question: The print model: cyan, magenta, yellow and…
questions.explanation: CMYK: K stands for key, the key black.

questions.question: Evenly spacing out or tightening letters across a word or line is…
questions.explanation: Kerning is a letter pair; tracking is the whole run of text.

questions.question: A panel that slides up from the bottom over the content is a…
questions.explanation: A sheet is a panel attached to the bottom edge of the screen.

questions.question: A short hint that appears when you hover over an icon is a…
questions.explanation: A tooltip must not hide important info: touchscreens have no hover.

questions.question: Elements placed close together read as a group. This Gestalt principle is…
questions.explanation: Spacing inside a group should be smaller than spacing between groups.

questions.question: Which shortcut adds Auto layout in Figma?
questions.explanation: Shift+A wraps the selection in a frame with Auto layout.
